The successful candidate will spend approximately 50% of their time in clinical work related to liver transplantation and transplant oncology. There might also be cross coverage of the kidney-pancreas inpatient service. The remaining time will be spent in research and teaching. The candidate will be appointed Clinician-Investigator and expected to develop an academic program in transplant oncology and related clinical and translational research. The desirable academic qualities of the successful candidate would include an appropriate graduate degree (MSc, PhD or equivalent), fellowship training, relevant grants, and publications and/or a proven track record and accomplishments in transplant oncology research consistent with a Clinician Investigator academic role. The candidate will also contribute to the clinical fellowship program in transplant hepatology, working alongside clinician educators within the group.

The Ajmera Transplant Centre performs 200 liver transplants annually. The successful candidate will join our existing group of five transplant hepatologists in the Ajmera Transplant Centre which is supported by a large multidisciplinary team of abdominal transplant surgeons, medical and surgical transplant fellows, nurse practitioners, nurse coordinators, allied health professionals and administrative staff.

The Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology of the UHN and SH is a group of 33 luminal gastroenterologists and hepatologists. The Division has active clinical and academic programs in many areas of gastroenterology and hepatology including viral hepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, fatty liver disease, portal hypertension, hepatocellular carcinoma and liver transplantation as well as IBD, nutrition, pancreatic cancer, neurogastroenterology and motility.

The UHN includes Toronto General, Toronto Western, Princess Margaret and Toronto Rehab Hospitals, as well as the Michener Institute. UHN is a Canada’s leading research academic hospital. Building on the strengths and reputation of each of its programs, UHN brings together the talent and resources needed to achieve global impact and provide exemplary patient care, research and education. SH is a health care organization comprised of Mount Sinai Hospital, Bridgepoint Active Healthcare and Circle of Care as an affiliate, extending SH’s continuum of care into home and community programs. The SH vision is to create a premier exemplar of an integrated health system for the future.

Depending on the academic rank, qualifications and experience, remuneration will be at least in the range of $250,000-$350,000 through the Department of Medicine's Academic Practice Plan. Medical and dental benefits are available. The successful candidate may be eligible to apply for a donor-named Professorship.

jobs.description_summary:
Humber River Health. Tomorrow’s Healthcare, Today.  

 

Humber River Health is a multi-site organization serving a population of more than 850,000 people in the northwest Greater Toronto Area. The organization is a member of the Toronto Academic Health Science Network (TAHSN) and operates Hennick H...
jobs.full_description_text:
Humber River Health. Tomorrow’s Healthcare, Today. 

 

Humber River Health is a multi-site organization serving a population of more than 850,000 people in the northwest Greater Toronto Area. The organization is a member of the Toronto Academic Health Science Network (TAHSN) and operates Hennick Humber Hospital, along with its Finch and Church campuses, supported by more than 5,000 employees, approximately 800 physicians, and over 600 volunteers.

 

Hennick Humber Hospital is North America’s first fully digital hospital. Through robotics and advanced technology, patients benefit from less pain, fewer complications, and shorter hospital stays. A custom combination of technology and clinical expertise supports a reimagined model of care focused on safety, efficiency, and improved outcomes. Its digital ecosystem includes automated laboratory services, medication management robotics, electronic health records, a Command Centre, computerized physician order entry, bedside computer terminals, and surgical tracking systems that keep families informed in real time.

 

These innovations enhance communication, improve efficiency, and create a more connected experience for patients and families.

 

This transformation has been made possible through the dedication of Humber’s staff, physicians, and volunteers. Together, they are united by a shared belief: the power to transform healthcare through innovation, collaboration, and excellence. With strong teams and a commitment to continuous improvement, Humber River Health continues to deliver Tomorrow’s Healthcare, Today.




We are looking for a:

 

Locum General Internist

 

Department and Program Overview

 

Department of Medicine

 

Position Summary

 

Hennick Humber Hospital, a leading academic community hospital, is seeking highly motivated and skilled General Internists to join our dynamic Internal Medicine Division, for assistance in covering a parental leave. The leave would be between November 1, 2026, to July 31, 2027.

 

As part of the General Internal Medicine group at HHH, you will be responsible for providing comprehensive care to patients in the outpatient and inpatient settings, managing a wide range of adult medical conditions, and contributing to the academic and educational mission of the institution. Humber’s affiliation with the University of Toronto and Queen’s University offers the opportunity to be a part of a vibrant academic community, working closely with residents, fellows, and medical students, while contributing to innovative clinical research projects. The ideal candidate will be passionate about general internal medicine and committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centered care to a diverse population.

 

The successful candidate would be expected to:

- Provide outpatient and inpatient care for adult patients with a broad range of medical conditions, including chronic diseases, acute illnesses, and preventive health.

- Conduct comprehensive evaluations, make diagnoses, and develop individualized treatment plans, integrating evidence-based medicine into daily practice.

- Manage patients with complex multi-system conditions, coordinating care with other specialties as needed.

- Participate in on-call rotations for inpatient care and ED admissions to GIM, providing weekend and after-hours coverage as needed.

- Participate in ambulatory clinics at HRH including Urgent Medical Care Clinic, Surgical Pre-Screening Clinic and OB Medicine Clinic.

- Offer patient education, counseling, and support to improve health outcomes and promote wellness.

 




Qualifications, Skills and Attributes

 

The successful applicant will be able to demonstrate experience in General Internal Medicine, managing complex inpatients, working with multidisciplinary teams, and participating in on-call shifts, outpatient clinics and other program-related activities.

 

In addition to demonstrated clinical excellence and outstanding interpersonal skills, candidates must be a qualified medical practitioner and a member of, or eligible for membership, with the College of Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process and employment. Please contact our recruitment team to discuss your needs confidentially.

 

This position is being posted in response to an existing vacancy at Humber River Health.

 

The hospital reserves the right not to appoint anyone to this position.

 

www.hrh.ca




﻿Interested Applicants

 

Applications will be accepted until August 15, 2026, however, the position will remain open until filled or recruitment is closed.

 

We encourage all interested candidates to apply in confidence by forwarding: (1) Letter of Interest and (2) up-to-date curriculum vitae 

 

Application package should be submitted to: 

 

Dr. Susan Tory

Chief of Medicine, Medical Director, Medicine Program & Command Centre

Humber River Health

1235 Wilson Avenue

Toronto, ON M3M 0B2

 

Send via email: ***@hrh.ca (🔒 Premium)

 

 

Why choose Humber River Health?

At Humber River Health, our staff, physicians, and volunteers are delivering Tomorrow's Healthcare, Today. We are proud to have been recognized as a part of Greater Toronto’s Top Employers by Mediacorp Canada Inc. We support employees by providing evidence-based leadership and cultivating a culture that consistently wows with our unwavering commitment to staff, physician and volunteer engagement. We are dedicated to high-quality patient care and demonstrate our values of compassion, professionalism, and respect.

 

Humber River Health is committed to creating an inclusive, equitable and accessible workplace that reflects the diversity of our communities. Guided by our strategic direction to embed equity, diversity and inclusion in everything we do – and to address systemic barriers – we foster a culture where everyone feels respected, valued and empowered to contribute.

 

We welcome applications from individuals of all equity-deserving groups, including Indigenous peoples, racialized communities, persons living with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ+ individuals and seniors. We recognize that diverse identities and perspectives strengthen our ability to deliver safe, innovative and compassionate care.

Clinic

Provis‑Rudd Clinic is a well‑established, high‑volume outpatient endoscopy centre located in downtown Toronto. Our clinic is equipped with modern endoscopy suites, advanced diagnostic technology, and a highly experienced team of nurses and support staff. We maintain strong referral networks and operate with streamlined workflows designed to support safe, efficient, and patient‑centred care. More information about our clinic can be found at ruddclinic.com.

 

Position

We are seeking qualified Gastroenterologists to join our outpatient endoscopy team. The ideal candidate brings strong procedural skills, a commitment to high‑quality patient care, and the ability to work collaboratively in a fast‑paced clinical environment. This role is well‑suited to physicians who prefer a procedural‑focused practice with minimal administrative burden.

 

Job Duties

Perform endoscopic procedures in accordance with clinical guidelines and clinic protocols
Conduct pre‑procedure assessments and provide post‑procedure care and instructions
Interpret findings and complete accurate, timely procedure reports
Collaborate with nursing and administrative teams to support efficient patient flow
Maintain high standards of infection control, safety, and quality assurance
Communicate effectively with referring physicians to support continuity of care
Participate in clinic‑wide quality initiatives and ongoing professional development
Support a respectful, patient‑centred environment aligned with clinic policies

 

Required Qualifications

Medical Degree from an accredited institution
Completion of 3 to 4 years of specialty residency training in gastroenterology
Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada certification (or eligibility)
Licensed or eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO)

· Proven experience in performing endoscopic procedures, including gastroscopy, colonoscopy, and related interventions

· Demonstrated expertise in patient evaluation, procedural planning, and post‑procedure management

· Strong knowledge of gastrointestinal disorders, clinical guidelines, and evidence‑based endoscopic techniques

Strong commitment to patient safety, quality care, and professional ethics
Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

 

Work Location 

Provis‑Rudd Clinic

123 Edward Street, Suite 400

Toronto, Ontario M5G 1E2

 

Hours

35 – 40 hours per week 

 

Employment Type

Permanent, Full-Time 

 

Wage

$300,000 – $500,000 CAD per year

 

Benefits

Benefits in accordance with provincial employment standards.

 

Language of Work

English

 

Contact

If you are qualified and interested in the position, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter to:

Jeanette Boltyansky

Director of Operations

Provis-Rudd Endoscopy Clinic

All inquiries will be handled confidentially.

Hospital for Sick Children, Division of Clinical and Metabolic Genetics

jobs.full_description_text:
Hospital for Sick Children, Division of Clinical and Metabolic Genetics

Effective July 1, 2027, the Department of Paediatrics, Temerity Faculty of Medicine at the University of Toronto and the Division of Clinical and Metabolic Genetics at The Hospital for Sick Children, 555 University Avenue, Toronto, Ontario, an academic health science centre dedicated exclusively to children, affiliated with the University of Toronto, is recruiting a full-time permanent academic clinician staff physician. 

The Division of Clinical and Metabolic Genetics has a long tradition of excellence in clinical care, education, and innovative research. Independent and collaborative clinical and basic research is performed by Division members. The Division hosts a residency training programs in addition to fellowship programs in Clinical Biochemical Genetics and Laboratory Biochemical Genetics, which are fully accredited by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada and the Canadian College of Medical Geneticists (CCMG). The Hospital for Sick Children has a full service biochemical diagnostic laboratory hosted within the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine.

The successful candidate will join a dynamic interprofessional care team. The successful candidate will provide care for clinical genetics patients in the outpatient settings and inpatient consultation service. Specific interest and expertise in methylation disorders, overgrowth and mechanisms of imprinting is preferred but not required. Experience with interpretation of results of long-read genome wide sequencing, RNA sequencing and methylation tests would be highly desirable. Evidence of excellence in teaching and research is required. Candidates at all career stages are encouraged to apply.

All candidates must be able to function proficiently in English, hold an MD, MBBS or equivalent thereto and be certified or eligible for certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or have comparable qualifications. Candidates must hold or be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. This position will remain open until filled.

The successful candidate will be eligible for an academic appointment at the University of Toronto. Rank and salary ($275,543 to $340,000) per annum will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will be eligible for a benefits package which includes medical, dental, life insurance, long term disability insurance, group insurance, pension plan, vision care, academic allowance, and a relocation package.

Interested individuals should submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae, and the names and addresses of three referees to: Dr. Roberto Mendoza, Head, Division of Clinical and Metabolic Genetics, Department of Paediatrics, email: ***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium) The Hospital for Sick Children, 555 University Avenue, Toronto, Ontario Canada M5G 1X8. 

The University of Toronto and The Hospital for Sick Children are strongly committed to diversity within its community. Both institutions recognize systemic barriers that impact equity seeking groups. As such, we welcome applications from historically marginalized groups including Black, Indigenous, and Racialized people, women, LGBTQIA+, and/or persons with disabilities. The Department recognizes and fairly considers the impact of leaves (e.g., family care or health-related) that may contribute to career interruptions or slowdowns. Candidates are encouraged to signal any leave that affected productivity, or that may have influenced their career path. This information will be considered to ensure the equitable assessment of the candidate’s record. The Department further supports an employment equity program and encourages members of designated equity groups to self-identify. It further seeks to ensure equitable treatment and full inclusion of persons with disabilities.

jobs.title: Dentist-in-Chief – Department of Paediatric Dentistry
jobs.description_summary:
The Department of Paediatric Dentistry at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), Faculty of Dentistry, University of Toronto, is inviting applications for the position of Dentist-in-Chief. This is a full-time role for an academic paediatric dentist and leader in paediatric oral health.

The effe...
jobs.full_description_text:
The Department of Paediatric Dentistry at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), Faculty of Dentistry, University of Toronto, is inviting applications for the position of Dentist-in-Chief. This is a full-time role for an academic paediatric dentist and leader in paediatric oral health.

The effective date of this appointment is June 2027 but can be negotiated.

Primary Description

Responsibilities include full clinical practice, research, and education, and administrative responsibilities as required by a Department Chief. Evidence of excellence in teaching and research is required. This role reports directly to the Chief of Peri-Operative Services.

Additional Description

The successful candidate should be a senior academic with an international reputation who can provide effective and collaborative leadership and vision at the hospital, provincial, national and international levels. The candidate must be eligible for appointment at the rank of Associate Professor at the University of Toronto and be eligible for certification with the Royal College of Dental Surgeons of Ontario. Candidates must obtain an appropriate Visa, if applicable.

We are seeking an individual whose leadership qualifications include management proficiency, dispute resolution, communications expertise, mentoring capabilities, the ability to engender trust, function collaboratively with all manner of clinical teams and administration. Additionally, the successful candidate will have a long-term vision for the Department which integrates with the mission of Peri-Operative Services, the Hospital and the University of Toronto.

Salary will be in the range of $200,000 to $400,000 for 40 hours per week, commensurate with qualifications and experience, and which will be supplemented by clinical billing activity. Benefits include Medical, Dental, Life, Group Insurance, Pension, Vision. A per annum stipend, in recognition of the administrative leadership responsibilities associated with the Department Chief role, will be provided. Support for relocation expenses will be offered. The position has a potential duration of two terms of five years each.

Department Description

The Department of Paediatric Dentistry at The Hospital for Sick Children consist of 18 dental surgeons, orthodontists and paediatric dentists, provides dental care for children and adolescents under 18 years whose treatment is best managed in a multidisciplinary hospital environment. It is integral to the Ontario Cleft Lip and Palate Craniofacial Dental program and is a major clinical training and research centre for the University of Toronto Graduate Paediatric Dentistry program. The Department also provides training to hospital staff, community dentists, physicians and families through affiliation with the University of Toronto.

Hospital Description

SickKids, located at 555 University Avenue in downtown Toronto, is among the largest children’s hospitals in North America and has a long history of excellence in clinical care, research and education. It was named the number one paediatric hospital in the world in 2025, by Newsweek magazine. SickKids is fully affiliated with the University of Toronto and is

located adjacent to the University campus and to numerous specialty hospitals and biomedical research institutes.

Toronto is a vibrant and multicultural city, widely recognized as one of the most diverse cities in the world, with approximately half of its residents born outside Canada and representation from more than 250 ethnicities. This diversity is reflected in the city’s neighbourhoods, food scene, Michelin-starred restaurants across Toronto and the surrounding region, and strengths in key sectors such as life sciences, finance, information, and communications technology. As one of the largest cities in North America, Toronto offers a dynamic downtown, diverse neighbourhoods, strong schools, and access to leading universities. It is regularly recognized in global city, travel, and liveability rankings. World-famous lake and wilderness country and year-round outdoor recreation are easily accessible, as are two hub airports for regional and international travel.

Application Process

Applications will be accepted until October 30, 2026. Should you be interested in this opportunity, please forward a one-page statement of interest [which includes the names and contact information for 3 referees] and curriculum vitae, in PDF format, via email to:

Dr. Abhaya V. Kulkarni

Chief, Peri-Operative Services and Chair of the Search Committee

175 Elizabeth St, Toronto, ON M5G 2G3

EMAIL: ***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium)

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.

For more information about the University of Toronto, Department of Paediatric Dentistry, please visit our home page at https://www.dentistry.utoronto.ca

Diversity Statement

The University of Toronto embraces Diversity and is building a culture of belonging that increases our capacity to effectively address and serve the interests of our global community. We strongly encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples, Black and racialized persons, women, persons with disabilities, and people of diverse sexual and gender identities. We value applicants who have demonstrated a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion and recognize that diverse perspectives, experiences, and expertise are essential to strengthening our academic mission.

Accessibility Statement

The University strives to be an equitable and inclusive community and proactively seeks to increase diversity among its community members. Our values regarding equity and diversity are linked with our unwavering commitment to excellence in the pursuit of our academic mission.

The University is committed to the principles of the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). As such, we strive to make our recruitment, assessment, and selection processes as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for applicants with disabilities.

If you require any accommodations at any point during the application and hiring process, please contact***@utoronto.ca (🔒 Premium).

jobs.title: Division Head, Haematology Oncology
jobs.description_summary: Join our team and be part of our bold new strategy for Precision Child Health, advancing discovery, prevention, and treatment for children worldwide. The Division of Haematology Oncology provides diagnostic services and specialist care for children and adolescents with cancer (paediatric oncology) a...
jobs.full_description_text:
Join our team and be part of our bold new strategy for Precision Child Health, advancing discovery, prevention, and treatment for children worldwide. The Division of Haematology Oncology provides diagnostic services and specialist care for children and adolescents with cancer (paediatric oncology) and nonmalignant blood diseases (paediatric haematology), as well as those receiving haematopoietic stem cell transplantation and cellular therapies.

The Division of Hematology Oncology is seeking a full-time permanent faculty position as Division Head, Haematology Oncology at the Hospital for Sick Children, 555 University Ave., Toronto, ON, which is an academic health science centre dedicated to the care of children affiliated with the Temerty Faculty of Medicine at the University of Toronto.

The Division offers a comprehensive subspecialty residency /fellowship program, attracting Canadian and international trainees to our Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada-accredited program in Paediatric Haematology-Oncology. There are also specialized fellowships offered across the division ranging from early phase trials and neuro-oncology to cancer genetics, late effects/survivorship, and stem cell transplantation/cellular therapy. Our interprofessional team provides comprehensive care and services across 5 sections (haematology, stem cell transplant/cellular therapies, leukemia/lymphoma, solid tumour, and neuro-oncology). Specialized multi-disciplinary programs include New Agents and Innovative Therapies (NAIT), Cancer Genetics, Long Term Follow-up, Bone Marrow Failure, Haemoglobinopathies and Thrombosis.

We are actively involved in clinical, translational, and basic science research related to blood disorders and cancer in children, with a focus on designing and participating in prospective clinical trials and delivering precision therapies to patients locally, provincially, and nationally.

The successful candidate will lead and mentor our diverse faculty and trainees, collaborate with allied health and nursing partners, and innovate with our scientists at the Research Institute. By championing clinical services, education, and research, you will advance our cancer and haematology programs and align academic activities with the Temerty Faculty of Medicine at the University of Toronto.

The successful candidate will provide care in both inpatient and ambulatory settings within the Division of Haematology-Oncology. 

This role supports the expansion of specialized clinical services and offers opportunities for creative and professional activities, as well as translational and basic research to improve evidence-based care. As Division Head, you will also serve as a strategic advisor and steward of philanthropic funds, influencing the Division's vision and serving as Head of the Garron Family Cancer Centre (GFCC). The GFCC enhances and integrates clinical, research, and educational activities to improve outcomes for children, adolescents, and young adults with cancer.

The successful candidate must possess leadership and mentoring experience, with a demonstrated track record in academic and research excellence.

The successful candidate will be eligible for an academic appointment at the University of Toronto. Rank and salary ($425,000-$525,000) per annum will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The successful candidate may also be eligible for a leadership stipend. The successful candidate will be eligible for a benefits package which includes medical, dental, life insurance, long term disability insurance, group insurance, pension plan, vision care, academic allowance, and relocation package and support services.

All candidates must be able to function proficiently in English, hold an MD, MBBS or equivalent thereto and be certified or eligible for certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or have comparable qualifications. Candidates must hold or be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. This position will remain open until filled.

Interested individuals should submit a letter of interest, curriculum vitae including a statement of research, education and clinical contribution, and names and addresses of three references to

Dr. Meredith Irwin, Professor and Chair, Department of Paediatrics, The Hospital for Sick Children, 555 University Avenue, Toronto, Ontario Canada M5G 1X8: e-mail ***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium)

The Department is strongly committed to diversity within its community and especially welcomes applications from racialized person/persons of colour, women, Indigenous / Aboriginal People of North America, persons with disabilities, LGBTQ persons, and others who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas. The Department recognizes and fairly considers the impact of leaves (e.g., family care or health-related) that may contribute to career interruptions or slowdowns. Candidates are encouraged to signal any leave that affected productivity, or that may have influenced their career path. This information will be considered to ensure the equitable assessment of the candidate’s record. The Department further supports an employment equity program and encourages members of designated equity groups to self-identify. It further seeks to ensure equitable treatment and full inclusion of persons with disabilities. Persons with disabilities who anticipate needing accommodations for any part of the application process may contact, in confidence, ***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium)

jobs.full_description_text:
Consultant Pediatrician – Locum Opportunity (Toronto, Ontario) We are seeking a Consultant Pediatrician to provide parental leave coverage from October 2026 to October 2027, with the opportunity to remain on as an associate following the locum period, if desired. This is an excellent opportunity to join a modern, well-established community practice with a strong referral base and the flexibility to build a practice that aligns with your professional interests. What we offer: Modern, clean, and bright clinical space Supportive, collegial, multidisciplinary environment including family medicine, subspecialty medicine, mental health, and allied health professionals Full-service administrative support Advanced technology including OSCAR Pro EMR, Ocean eReferrals, and AI scribe tools Established referral network that can support a busy practice from day one Flexible scheduling with the ability to set your own hours Extremely competitive income split Free parking and easy access via public transit Practice Profile The current practice is a 100% consultative pediatric practice with a mix of medical, developmental, and mental health consultations. Follow-up care is provided at the discretion of the consultant pediatrician. For physicians interested in continuing beyond the locum period, there is an opportunity to remain as an associate and further develop the practice based on individual interests, including focused areas of pediatrics, developmental care, mental health, or primary care services. Located in the vibrant Mimico community of Toronto, this opportunity combines professional flexibility, strong clinical support, and immediate access to a well-established patient base.




Requirements:

Board certification in Pediatrics
CPSO license in Pediatrics
Excellent communication skills for effective collaboration with medical teams.
Commitment to delivering high-quality, patient-centered care.

Why Mimico Medical?

Physician-owned and operated.
State-of-the-art medical facilities with advanced technology.
Supportive work environment prioritizing physician quality of life.
Opportunities for professional growth and autonomy.
Full management support from an experienced team.
Competitive compensation and billing support.

About Us

Mimico Medical is a growing multidisciplinary medical clinic proudly serving the Etobicoke community with comprehensive, patient-centered healthcare. Our team includes 9 Family Physicians operating under the FHO+ care model, supported by a robust internal referral network and allied health services, including Psychiatry, Psychotherapy, Physiotherapy, Pediatrics, Women's Health, and other specialty clinics. As we continue to expand our services, we are committed to improving access to high-quality, collaborative care for our patients.

Midtown: Bathurst and St Clair

North York: Leslie and 401

 

DAYTIME OR AFTER-HOURS POSITIONS AVAILABLE

 

The offices are brand new. The EMR is PS Suite (Telus).

Our professional office staff handles all the administrative tasks.

 

Kidcrew is an award-winning multi-disciplinary pediatric practice located in Midtown Toronto and North York. We have over 80,000 patients.

 

Our Virtual Care Clinic serves kids from anywhere in Ontario.

Our virtual-care model provides flexibility to allow doctors to augment with casual, part-time, or full-time work.

Cloud-based, HIPAA/PHIPA compliant EMR with VPN access from home.

Chart, bill, order labs/imaging/write sick notes/referrals and discharge notes from anywhere you want!

Guaranteed patient volume (4-6/hr) depending on preference. 

ZERO EMR fee.

Competitive overhead rate.

Overhead is tax-deductible as an associate (versus an employee at other clinics).

Bill upwards of $500/hour

Commitment is casual or long-term. You can pick up as much or as little as you want. When you want to work, how long, and how frequently you see patients, it's up to you.

Our professional office staff handles all the administrative tasks.

 

Who do we serve?

We can see patients from anywhere in Ontario, including in rural, northern, and underserviced areas. Telemedicine can improve the health and well-being of patients who have poor access to care or can only use the ER. We can help improve access and, therefore, patients' overall health and well-being in these areas. We are thrilled to help more families with timely expert pediatric care.

 

Patient Follow Up

Kidcrew clinicians collaborate to ensure patients have timely and accessible follow-up, in order to avoid unnecessary emergency room use and ensure continuity of care.

 

Flexible patient encounters: urgent visits, consults or follow-ups, in person or via virtual medicine.

 

Flexibility in hours: the ability to work part-time, FT, evenings, or weekends 

 

Work alongside specialists: with over 20 different medical and surgical specialties affiliated

 

Attractive fee split

 

Requirement: CPSO licensed

This is an excellent opportunity to build or relocate a practice in a highly populated residential area.

The clinic is open seven days a week.

**New Graduates Encouraged to Apply**

 

About Kidcrew

At Kidcrew, we have created forward-thinking and innovative children's clinics focusing on family-centred care and wellness for children of all ages. We are looking to bring on excellent, eager, and friendly pediatricians and specialists. Pediatricians will provide well-baby care, sick visits, and general pediatrics to this thriving community. In addition, the clinic provides nursing care.

We are passionate about providing quality pediatric care for kids and families. A state-of-the-art EMR is used along with well-qualified friendly, trained support staff. 

From our friendly front desk staff to our non-traditional 2,000 square-foot patient lounges with a playground, iPad stations, and a playroom, Kidcrew is committed to providing an exceptional patient experience. We have over 120 clinicians on our team: pediatricians, a variety of pediatric sub-specialists, dietitians, speech-language pathologists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, psychologists, and others to provide a comprehensive and collaborative model under one roof. 

Join us on our journey to reinventing kids' healthcare.

https://kidcrew.com/

 

Our founder, Dr Dina Kulik, is happy to review opportunities at ***@kidcrew.com (🔒 Premium)

jobs.title: Staff Echocardiographer Cardiologist
jobs.description_summary:
Staff Paediatric Cardiologist

Effective immediately The Division of Cardiology at The Hospital for Sick Children, Department of Paediatrics (555 University Ave. Toronto, M5G 1X9), an academic health science centre dedicated exclusively to children, affiliated with the University of Toronto, is seek...
jobs.full_description_text:
Staff Paediatric Cardiologist

Effective immediately The Division of Cardiology at The Hospital for Sick Children, Department of Paediatrics (555 University Ave. Toronto, M5G 1X9), an academic health science centre dedicated exclusively to children, affiliated with the University of Toronto, is seeking a full-time permanent faculty position for a staff paediatric cardiologist with sub-specialty training in Echocardiography at the Labatt Family Heart Centre – Cardiology Division. Candidates with expertise in Fetal Cardiology or Pulmonary Hypertension would be of special interest.

The Labatt Family Heart Centre brings together significant interdisciplinary and inter-professional activities within Paediatric Cardiology, Cardiovascular (CV) Surgery, Cardiac Critical Care, Cardiovascular Research and Adult Congenital Heart Disease Programs, thus allowing the Heart Centre to address the needs of patients and families from fetal life to adulthood. The Heart Centre at The Hospital for Sick Children promotes these activities through seamless integration of research activities, academic performance, and exemplary clinical care.

The primary role of the successful candidate will be to focus on providing excellence in clinical care, education, and research in the field of Echocardiography. The successful candidate will also be expected to teach our fellows and undertake innovative and impactful research. We anticipate some requirement for additional service provision in other subspecialty areas, including general inpatient and outpatient cardiology, depending on the candidate’s experience and interests.

The successful applicant would ideally have completed subspecialty training and/or specific clinical experience in echocardiography and fetal cardiology and will report to the Division Head, Labatt Family Heart Centre. The successful candidate must be able to function proficiently in English, hold an MD, MBBS or the equivalent thereto and be certified or eligible for certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or have comparable qualifications. Candidates must hold or be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. The successful candidate must be eligible for an academic appointment at the University of Toronto. Rank and salary ($300,000-$450,000) per annum and will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae and a statement outlining current and future clinical and research interests. In addition, provide names and addresses of three references to Dr. Mike Seed, Head, Division of Cardiology, Department of Paediatrics, Hospital for Sick Children 555 University Avenue, Toronto, Ontario, Canada M5G 1X8 email: ***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium)

For additional information regarding the Department of Paediatrics see http://www.sickkids.ca/paediatrics/.

The University of Toronto and The Hospital for Sick Children are strongly committed to diversity within its community. Both institutions recognize systemic barriers that impact equity seeking groups. As such, we welcome applications from historically marginalized groups including Black, Indigenous, and Racialized people, women, LGBTQIA+, and/or persons with disabilities. The Department recognizes and fairly considers the impact of leaves (e.g., family care or health-related) that may contribute to career interruptions or slowdowns. Candidates are encouraged to signal any leave that affected productivity, or that may have influenced their career path. This information will be considered to ensure the equitable assessment of the candidate’s record. The Department further supports an employment equity program and encourages members of designated equity groups to self-identify. It further seeks to ensure equitable treatment and full inclusion of persons with disabilities. Persons with disabilities who anticipate needing accommodations for any part of the application process may contact, in confidence, Anna Capizzano, r at ***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium) or***-***-**** (🔒 Premium).

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply; however, in accordance with Canadian immigration requirements, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. Only those applicants selected for the interview will be contacted.

The successful candidate must be able to function proficiently in English, hold an MD, MBBS or the equivalent thereto and be certified or eligible for certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or have comparable qualifications. Candidates must hold or be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. The successful candidate must be eligible for an academic appointment at the University of Toronto. Rank and salary ($300,000-$450,000) per annum and will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae and a statement outlining current and future clinical and research interests. In addition, provide names and addresses of three references to Dr. Mike Seed, Head, Division of Cardiology, Department of Paediatrics, Hospital for Sick Children 555 University Avenue, Toronto, Ontario, Canada M5G 1X8 email: mike.seed@sickkids.ca For additional information regarding the Department of Paediatrics see http://www.sickkids.ca/paediatrics/ . The University of Toronto and The Hospital for Sick Children are strongly committed to diversity within its community. Both institutions recognize systemic barriers that impact equity seeking groups. As such, we welcome applications from historically marginalized groups including Black, Indigenous, and Racialized people, women, LGBTQIA+, and/or persons with disabilities. The Department recognizes and fairly considers the impact of leaves (e.g., family care or health-related) that may contribute to career interruptions or slowdowns. Candidates are encouraged to signal any leave that affected productivity, or that may have influenced their career path. This information will be considered to ensure the equitable assessment of the candidate’s record. The Department further supports an employment equity program and encourages members of designated equity groups to self-identify. It further seeks to ensure equitable treatment and full inclusion of persons with disabilities. Persons with disabilities who anticipate needing accommodations for any part of the application process may contact, in confidence, Anna Capizzano, r at meagan.cameira@sickkids.ca or 416.613.6122. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply; however, in accordance with Canadian immigration requirements, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. Only those applicants selected for the interview will be contacted.

jobs.full_description_text:
Child Respirology - full-time or part-time, wanted for our multi-disciplinary clinic at Bathurst and St Clair and North York location on Duncan Mill Road. 

DAYTIME OR AFTER-HOURS POSITIONS AVAILABLE

The offices are brand new. The EMR is PS Suite (Telus).

Our professional office staff handles all the administrative tasks.

Part-time, full-time, or casual, wanted for our large, collaborative, multidisciplinary clinic.

Kidcrew is an award-winning multidisciplinary pediatric practice located at Bathurst and St Clair in Midtown Toronto.

We have over 70,000 patients.

Our Virtual Care Clinic serves kids from anywhere in Ontario.

Our virtual-care model provides flexibility to allow doctors to augment with casual, part-time, or full-time work.

Cloud-based, HIPAA/PHIPA compliant EMR with VPN access from home.

Chart, bill, order labs/imaging/write sick notes/referrals and discharge notes from anywhere you want!

Guaranteed patient volume depending on preference. 

ZERO EMR fee.

Competitive overhead rate.

Overhead is tax-deductible as an associate (versus an employee at other clinics).

Commitment is casual or long-term. You can pick up as much or as little as you want. When you want to work, how long, and how frequently you see patients, it's up to you.

Our professional office staff handles all the administrative tasks.

Who do we serve?

We can see patients from anywhere in Ontario, including in rural, northern, and underserviced areas. Telemedicine can improve the health and well-being of patients who have poor access to care or can only use the ER. We are thrilled to help more families with timely expert pediatric care.

Patient Follow Up

As we have a brick-and-mortar location, if you want a patient examined, one of the Kidcrew colleagues can accommodate seeing a patient for a follow-up, avoid emergency room use and ensure continuity of care.

Flexible patient encounters: sick visits, consults or follow-ups, in person or via telemedicine

Flexibility in hours: the ability to work part-time, FT, evenings, or weekends 

Work alongside specialists: with over 20 different medical and surgical specialties affiliated

Attractive fee split

Requirement: CPSO licensed

This is an excellent opportunity to build or relocate a practice in a highly populated residential area.

The clinic is open seven days a week.

**New Graduates Encouraged to Apply**

About Kidcrew

At Kidcrew, we have created a forward-thinking and innovative children's clinic focusing on family-centered care and wellness for children of all ages. We are looking to bring on excellent, eager, and friendly pediatricians and specialists. Pediatricians will provide well-baby care, sick visits, and general pediatrics to this thriving community. In addition, the clinic provides nursing care.

We are passionate about providing quality pediatric care for kids and families. A state-of-the-art EMR is used along with well-qualified friendly, trained support staff. 

From our friendly front desk staff to our non-traditional 2,000 square-foot patient lounge with a playground, iPad stations, and a playroom, Kidcrew is committed to providing an exceptional patient experience. We have over 120 clinicians on our team: pediatricians, a variety of pediatric sub-specialists, dietitians, speech-language pathologists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, psychologists, and others to provide a comprehensive and collaborative model under one roof. 

Join us on our journey in reinventing kids' healthcare.

jobs.description_summary: Effective immediately, a permanent full-time faculty position as a Clinician Scientist is available in the Division of Nephrology, Department of Paediatrics, at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), 555 University Avenue, Toronto, ON, Canada. The new faculty member will also be appointed in the...
jobs.full_description_text:
Effective immediately, a permanent full-time faculty position as a Clinician Scientist is available in the Division of Nephrology, Department of Paediatrics, at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), 555 University Avenue, Toronto, ON, Canada. The new faculty member will also be appointed in the Research Institute at The Hospital for Sick Children.

SickKids is a world-renowned academic health science centre dedicated to the care of children, affiliated with the University of Toronto. The SickKids Research Institute includes seven fully integrated research programs (http://www.sickkids.ca/Research/) and is in the state-of-the-art Peter Gilgan Centre for Research & Learning, within the Toronto Discovery District. The position offers a unique environment for medical science discoveries near nine teaching and research hospitals and Canada’s largest university. 

The Division of Nephrology comprises fifteen highly collegial full-and part-time faculty committed to world-leading clinical care spanning the entire field of Pediatric Nephrology, including high volume dialysis/apheresis and transplant programs and high-impact clinical and basic research focused on childhood and rare kidney diseases, aligning with SickKids' “Precision Child Health” initiative.

The successful candidate should have a strong background in basic science, preferably with expertise in areas such as multi-omics, gene editing, disease modelling, or drug discovery. They should have substantial research experience, typically demonstrated through a PhD and/or postdoctoral training, along with a strong publication record, successful grant funding, and conference presentations. Preference will be given to candidates focused on rare kidney diseases. The successful applicant will also be expected to apply for a scientist-track role at the SickKids Research Institute and build an impactful research career within an equitable and inclusive environment.

The candidate’s responsibilities will involve teaching and mentoring students across the division, department, and university. The successful candidate should qualify for a cross-appointment with a University of Toronto graduate program to supervise graduate students directly. Strong collaboration with colleagues across the division, department, research institute, university, external partners, and the broader community is also expected.

The successful candidate will contribute to both research and clinical care, with 20–30% of responsibilities dedicated to patient care. The ideal applicant will demonstrate comprehensive clinical expertise in Pediatric Nephrology, including chronic kidney disease (CKD), renal replacement therapy, and kidney transplantation.

The successful candidate will be eligible for an academic appointment at the University of Toronto. Rank and salary ($275,000-$352,000) will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will be eligible for a benefits package that includes medical, dental, life insurance, long-term disability insurance, group insurance, pension plan, vision care, academic allowance, and a relocation package.

All candidates must be able to function proficiently in English, hold an MD, MBBS or equivalent degree, and be certified (or eligible for certification) by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or have comparable qualifications. Candidates must hold (or be eligible for) licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario.

Interested individuals should submit a letter of application and curriculum vitae with the names and addresses of three references to the attention of Dr. Christoph Licht, Head, Division of Nephrology, Department of Paediatrics, c/o Linda Correia, Sr. Manager, Department of Paediatrics, The Hospital for Sick Children, 555 University Avenue, Toronto, ON M5G 1X8, Canada; email: ***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium).

Visit our website for additional information regarding the Department of Paediatrics: www.paeds.utoronto.ca

The University of Toronto and The Hospital for Sick Children are strongly committed to diversity within their community. Both institutions recognize systemic barriers that impact equity-seeking groups. As such, we welcome applications from historically marginalized groups, including Black, Indigenous, and Racialized people, women, LGBTQIA+, and/or persons with disabilities. The Department recognizes and fairly considers the impact of leaves (e.g., family care or health-related) that may contribute to career interruptions or slowdowns. Candidates are encouraged to disclose any leave that affected productivity or that may have influenced their career path. This information will be considered to ensure the equitable assessment of the candidate’s record. The Department further supports an employment equity program and encourages members of designated equity groups to self-identify. It further seeks to ensure equitable treatment and full inclusion of persons with disabilities.

jobs.title: Paediatric Haematology/ Oncologist
jobs.description_summary: Effective October 1, 2026, the Division of Haematology/Oncology, Blood and Marrow Transplant/Cellular Therapy (BMT/CT) Section, at the Hospital for Sick Children, (SickKids), Department of Paediatrics, 555 University Avenue. Toronto, ON which is an academic health science centre dedicated to the car...
jobs.full_description_text:
Effective October 1, 2026, the Division of Haematology/Oncology, Blood and Marrow Transplant/Cellular Therapy (BMT/CT) Section, at the Hospital for Sick Children, (SickKids), Department of Paediatrics, 555 University Avenue. Toronto, ON which is an academic health science centre dedicated to the care of children; a fully affiliated hospital within the University of Toronto is recruiting a permanent full-time Paediatric Haematology/ Oncologist. 

The Blood and Marrow Transplant/Cellular Therapy program at SickKids is one of the largest and most active paediatric transplant and cellular therapy programs in North America. We are FACT-accredited with a 17-bed dedicated inpatient unit, performing approximately 120-130 transplants and cellular therapy procedures annually for children referred from across Ontario and the Atlantic provinces. Our clinical scope includes transplantation and cell-based therapies for the treatment of malignancies, immunodeficiencies, bone marrow failure syndromes, metabolic disorders, autoimmune diseases and haemoglobinopathies.

The section currently comprises of six faculty members with a robust portfolio of gene therapy, cell therapy, and immune effector cell clinical trials, as well as active translational and basic research programs. The program is developing on-site cell- and gene therapy manufacturing capabilities and benefits from close collaboration with SickKids' internationally recognized programs in immunology, haemoglobinopathy, metabolic disease, and oncology.

With rapidly expanding indications for cellular therapies including CAR-T, gene therapy, and gene editing, the successful candidate will not only contribute to our clinical excellence but help shape the strategic direction of the program over the next decade.

SickKids is home to Canada's largest paediatric research institute, with more than 2,000 researchers, trainees, and staff. The BMT/CT section is embedded within this vibrant research community, with extensive opportunities for collaboration across the SickKids Research Institute, the University of Toronto, and affiliated networks. Significant philanthropic support is dedicated to advancing the program's clinical and research mission.

The BMT/CT section operates a well-established clinical fellowship program that attracts trainees from Canada and around the world. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to contribute to the education of the next generation of transplant and cellular therapy physicians, with a commitment to global capacity-building in the field.

The successful candidate will join a dynamic interprofessional care team. The successful candidate will provide care for patients in the BMT/CT section of the Division in the inpatient and ambulatory settings with responsibilities which include procedures and participation in out-of-hours clinical coverage. The successful candidate is expected to spend most of their time devoted to clinical service and to making important contributions to the clinical, research and teaching missions of the Division. Evidence of excellence in teaching and research is required. Candidates at all career stages are encouraged to apply.

All candidates must be able to function proficiency in English, hold an MD, MBBS or equivalent thereto and be certified or eligible for certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or have comparable qualifications. Candidates must hold or be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. 

The successful candidate must be eligible for an academic appointment at the University of Toronto. Rank and salary will be ($275,543-$350,000) per annum, commensurate with qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will be eligible for a benefit package which includes medical, dental, life insurance, long term disability insurance, group insurance, pension plan, vision care, academic allowance, and a relocation package.

Interested individuals should send a letter of application, curriculum vitae and the names and addresses of three referees to Dr. James Whitlock, Head, Division of Hematology/Oncology, Hospital for Sick Children, 555 University Avenue, Toronto, Canada M5G1X8 (***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium)).

Visit our Web site or for additional information regarding the Department of Paediatrics, and see www.paeds.utoronto.ca

The University of Toronto and The Hospital for Sick Children are strongly committed to diversity within its community. Both institutions recognize systemic barriers that impact equity seeking groups. As such, we welcome applications from historically marginalized groups including Black, Indigenous, and Racialized people, women, LGBTQIA+, and/or persons with disabilities. The Department recognizes and fairly considers the impact of leaves (e.g., family care or health-related) that may contribute to career interruptions or slowdowns. Candidates are encouraged to signal any leave that affected productivity, or that may have influenced their career path. This information will be considered to ensure the equitable assessment of the candidate’s record. The Department further supports an employment equity program and encourages members of designated equity groups to self-identify. It further seeks to ensure equitable treatment and full inclusion of persons with disabilities. Persons with disabilities who anticipate needing accommodations for any part of the application process may contact, in confidence, Sarah Isbester, Executive Assistant to the Chair at ***@sickkids.ca (🔒 Premium) or***-***-**** (🔒 Premium).

jobs.title: Psychiatrist needed for CFB Toronto
jobs.description_summary: Calian is proud to continue a long-standing contractual relationship with the Department of National Defence (DND) to provide healthcare services to the Canadian Armed Forces. Through the Health Care Provider Contract, Calian employs health care professionals across Canada who are integral to suppor...
jobs.full_description_text:
Calian is proud to continue a long-standing contractual relationship with the Department of National Defence (DND) to provide healthcare services to the Canadian Armed Forces. Through the Health Care Provider Contract, Calian employs health care professionals across Canada who are integral to supporting the health and wellbeing of our military members.

 

Position Overview

Calian is seeking a part-time Psychiatrist to provide clinical services to Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) members at Canadian Forces Base Toronto. As a psychiatrist in this exclusive clinic, you’ll be part of a team of mental health professionals providing high quality care.

Up to 0.4 FTE is available during clinic operation from Monday to Friday.

 

Responsibilities

• Conducting psychiatric assessments, providing diagnosis based on DSM, and providing treatment of a variety of mental health conditions including trauma-related disorders, depressive disorders, anxiety disorders, substance-related disorder, and addictive disorders.

• Prepares detailed written psychiatric assessment reports on referred patients, including recommendations for a treatment plan, and participates in the implementation of the treatment plan by providing psychotherapy, prescribing appropriate somatic therapy, and generating patient medical records to support the multidisciplinary team.

• Advising on operational readiness, return to work, prognosis, impairment, and restrictions.

• Conducting psychopharmacological treatment, conducting evidence-based therapy such as CBT, responding to emergencies, and crisis.

• Conducting tele-medicine assessments and interventions.

• Providing clinical preceptorship and educational sessions for staff.

• Participates as a member of the multidisciplinary mental health team in case reviews.

• Provides expert advice on mental illness or disorders to primary care providers to assist them in the identification, diagnosis, and treatment of patients with mental health disorders.

• Creates and maintains patient records.

 

Qualifications

• Registered with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario

• Specialty certification in psychiatry from the Royal College of Physicians of Canada in Psychiatry (FRCPC)

• Experience providing psychiatric services to an adult population 18-60 years of age

• Experience providing pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy with individuals using evidence-based therapy such as CBT

• Experience in delivering psychiatric services for a wide range of mental illnesses

 

Additional Requirements

• You will be able to obtain a Government Security Clearance at the Reliability level

jobs.full_description_text:
St. Joseph's Health Centre, Toronto, is seeking psychiatrists with a minimum of 3 years' experience for general adult psychiatry services. We deliver care to a diverse and often marginalized population in a collaborative and dynamic multidisciplinary setting with support from mental health clinicians and case managers. We aim to deliver a time-limited intensive episode of care in the outpatient clinic aimed at reintegrating patients with appropriate community supports. The Department offers an exciting range of psychiatric services including rTMS, ECT, urgent care child & adolescent clinic, adult urgent care, ACTT, group psychotherapy modalities, Day Treatment Program, and inpatient services for children and adolescents, transitional age youth, and the general adult population.




Position Description: Full-time (1.0 FTE) general psychiatry services in the adult psychiatry setting. One position is permanent full-time (mixed ambulatory and acute care) while the other is a 10-month locum position (ambulatory care). Proficiency in concurrent disorders is an asset (roughly 25% of time doing concurrent disorders work).




Remuneration: Includes a combination of OHIP billings, on-call stipend (HOCC), a generous base stipend, and educational funds for contributions to medical education and training. There are currently no overhead expenses.




Requirements & Qualifications:

Minimum 3 years' experience in general adult psychiatry.
Active certificate of registration from the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO).
Fellowship / certification from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (FRCPC).
Permanent staff must be eligible for a university appointment with the University of Toronto Temerty Faculty of Medicine.




Equity & Diversity Statement: The University of Toronto and Unity Health Toronto are strongly committed to diversity within their community and especially welcome applications from racialized persons/persons of colour, women, Indigenous/Aboriginal People of North America, persons with disability, 2SLGBTQ+ persons, and others who may contribute to enhancing cultural safety in care and further diversification of ideas. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.

jobs.full_description_text:
Part-Time Psychiatrist – (Virtual Consultations)

Flexible Remote Opportunity | Competitive Compensation Hybrid of OHIP + Stipend




Our outpatient community Rapid Access Addiction Medicine (RAAM) clinic is actively seeking a psychiatrist to join our team on a part-time, virtual basis.




This is an ideal opportunity for a psychiatrist who wants to fit meaningful, well-compensated clinical work into an existing schedule. We offer the flexibility to choose when to see patients. Since most patients are admitted to a residential treatment facility, consults can fit throughout your day (e.g., during a no-show to your regular practice), ensuring no lost income during your workday.




Your scope will be limited to the psychiatric assessment and treatment of patients engaged in a formal addiction treatment program. All patients are managed collaboratively with our team of Addiction Medicine Physicians, counselors, and psychotherapists in a high-quality, patient-centred environment.




Experience and/or training in addictions psychiatry is an asset but not a requirement, as our collaborative team can provide guidance and mentorship in addiction medicine.




Duties include:




 - Conducting virtual psychiatric assessments

 - Developing treatment and care plans

 - Prescribing medication(s) where appropriate

 - Supporting patients with substance use and concurrent disorders

 - Identifying safety concerns and referring to the ER when needed

 - Collaborating with other healthcare professionals

 - Maintaining appropriate clinical documentation and standards of care




We are looking for a licensed psychiatrist with:




 - Strong clinical judgment and excellent communication skills

 - A compassionate, patient-centred approach

 - Comfort providing care through a virtual platform

 - The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with a broader clinical team




About our clinic:




Comprehensive Treatment Clinic (CTC) is a new kind of addictions clinic focused on whole-person care. We offer treatment for persons using all kinds of substances. Our services include medication, counseling, art groups, affordable psychotherapy, harm reduction supplies, and more.




Contact us at ***@ctctoronto.com (🔒 Premium) or***-***-**** (🔒 Premium) for more information.

Website: http://www.ctctoronto.com

Field Trip Health is expanding its medical team across Ontario, British Columbia, and Quebec, and we’re seeking psychiatrists who want to be part of one of North America’s most experienced and outcomes-informed KAP programs.




KAP offers patients a powerful opportunity for meaningful therapeutic change — often helping individuals move forward when traditional treatments have plateaued. At Field Trip, psychiatrists are supported by a deeply collaborative care team and a clinical model built on safety, compassion, and evidence-based practice.




Why Field Trip:

Expertise you can trust: Field Trip is a leader in psychedelic-assisted therapies, with thousands of KAP sessions delivered and continuously refined care pathways.
Training provided: Comprehensive onboarding and ongoing clinical support from experienced nurses, therapists, and medical leadership.
Flexible, negotiable structure: Part-time, hybrid or virtual — tailored to your interests and availability with guaranteed sessional rates.
No overhead costs: We provide full administrative, scheduling, and documentation support.
Collaborative, values-aligned environment: Work alongside psychiatrists, nurses, and psychotherapists committed to clinical excellence and patient safety.
Opportunities to shape the future of care: Contribute to evolving treatment models and practice-informed clinical research.

To learn more, please contact Dr. Adam Blackman at ***@fieldtriphealth.ca (🔒 Premium). Website: fieldtriphealth.ca

jobs.title: Geriatric Psychiatrist - Clinician Teacher - University Health Network
jobs.company: University Health Network Mental Health Program
jobs.description_summary: The UHN Mental Health Program and Seniors Mental Health Division is seeking to recruit a Clinician-Teacher to be based at Toronto General Hospital. The successful applicant should be eligible for a full-time clinical academic appointment in the Department of Psychiatry, Faculty of Medicine at the Un...
jobs.full_description_text:
The UHN Mental Health Program and Seniors Mental Health Division is seeking to recruit a Clinician-Teacher to be based at Toronto General Hospital. The successful applicant should be eligible for a full-time clinical academic appointment in the Department of Psychiatry, Faculty of Medicine at the University of Toronto. The position is available from November 1, 2026, with the start date flexible and negotiable based on the successful candidate's availability. 

The Seniors Mental Health Division at UHN provides services for seniors across UHN in multiple clinical settings. Inpatient services include: consultation to acute care medical and surgical units, geriatric psychiatry inpatient beds (Toronto General Hospital), and the Specialized Dementia Unit (Toronto Rehab). Outpatient services include: The University Health Network Memory Clinic (Toronto Western Hospital and Toronto Rehab), and Seniors Mental Health outpatient clinics (Toronto General Hospital and West Park). There are also a number of outreach programs, including mental health services to long term care homes, UHN transitional and complex continuing care sites, the Virtual Behavioural Medicine program, and the Independence at Home program. 

We have an opportunity for a geriatric psychiatrist to be based at Toronto General Hospital (TGH). TGH is one of Canada's leading acute care hospitals and is internationally recognized for excellence in medicine, surgery, and transplantation, serving a diverse downtown Toronto community. 

There are three key areas of clinical need within Seniors Mental Health at UHN: 1) providing geriatric psychiatry Consultation-Liaison (C-L) services at TGH; 2) delivering outreach mental health services to long-term care homes affiliated with UHN; 3) providing coverage for the Virtual Behavioural Medicine program and the Specialized Dementia Unit at Toronto Rehab. The applicant should have an interest in practicing in at least two of these areas of geriatric psychiatry. 

The successful applicant must hold MD and FRCPC qualifications (or applied for the FRCPC examination in psychiatry) and have or be eligible for licensure as a psychiatrist in the province of Ontario as stipulated by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO). The successful candidate is also required to have subspecialty clinical training in geriatric psychiatry and be eligible to apply for or have completed the Royal College Geriatric Psychiatry subspecialty examination. 

This position offers a strong combination of clinical and academic responsibilities, including opportunities to contribute to the development and evaluation of innovative models of care, service improvement initiatives, and quality enhancement projects. Applicants with a demonstrated academic interest in geriatric consultation-liaison psychiatry are particularly encouraged to apply. 

The successful candidate will also participate in teaching and mentorship across undergraduate, graduate, postgraduate, and fellowship training programs. Experience in teaching and supervising learners in geriatric psychiatry is considered an asset. 

Academic rank, salary, and contractual arrangements will be commensurate with the qualifications and experience of the successful candidate. Compensation will depend on the volume of clinical work performed and is based on a fee-for-service billing model. Total remuneration is expected to be within the typical range for an experienced psychiatrist practicing in Ontario. 

Depending on the final role and job description, additional support may be available for protected academic, research, and program development time through a variety of funding mechanisms within UHN Mental Health. 

Interested individuals should send a covering letter and copy of their curriculum vitae to: Dr. Andrea Iaboni, Medical Lead, Seniors Mental Health, UHN Mental Health at email ***@uhn.ca (🔒 Premium)

The University Health Network and the University of Toronto are strongly committed to diversity within their communities and especially welcome applications from visible minority group members, women, Aboriginal persons, persons with disabilities, members of sexual minority groups, and others who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.

jobs.description_summary:
About the Centre for Psychodynamic Insights:

The Centre for Psychodynamic Insights is a virtual psychotherapy clinic based in Toronto, Ontario, specializing in psychodynamic psychotherapy. Our approach is rooted in evidence-based interventions and focuses on uncovering, understanding, and resolving...
jobs.full_description_text:
About the Centre for Psychodynamic Insights:

The Centre for Psychodynamic Insights is a virtual psychotherapy clinic based in Toronto, Ontario, specializing in psychodynamic psychotherapy. Our approach is rooted in evidence-based interventions and focuses on uncovering, understanding, and resolving the underlying emotions and root causes of symptoms. Through in-depth, collaborative discussions, we analyze unconscious thoughts and emotions from childhood to the present, exploring how they influence current experiences. This comprehensive approach allows us to develop targeted strategies that foster meaningful change and symptom relief. At the Centre for Psychodynamic Insights, we are committed to helping patients achieve deeper self-awareness and lasting transformation through a personalized and integrative treatment plan.

About the Position:

This role is ideal for a psychiatrist with expertise in psychodynamic or psychoanalytic therapy who values in-depth, long-term therapeutic engagement. In addition to providing comprehensive psychotherapy, you will conduct thorough psychiatric assessments, prescribe psychotropic medications when appropriate, and monitor patients’ responses and side effects over time. You will also provide psychoeducation about medication use within a psychodynamically informed treatment framework. Working virtually with adolescents and adults (16+), you will address a broad range of concerns including trauma, neurodevelopmental conditions, personality disorders, and complex relational or sexual issues.

Requirements:

Conduct psychiatric assessments
Prescribe psychotropic medications and conduct regular assessments of therapeutic responses and side effects, and educate patients regarding psychotropic medication.
Provide psychodynamic/psychoanalytic therapy to adolescents and adults (16+). All theoretical frameworks are welcome (e.g., Jungian, Freudian, Object Relations, or Adlerian approaches).
Experience, comfort, and willingness in most of the specializations listed on our website. Experience working with trauma, anxiety, depression, neurodevelopmental disorders, personality disorders, and sexual issues is required.
Willingness to work with patients at a frequency of at least once a week.
Comfort using Avaros for scheduling, documentation, and secure communication.
Work virtually with access to a confidential workspace, adequate lighting, high-speed internet, and a high-quality camera.
Ability to maintain a caseload of at least 8 patients per week.

Qualifications:

For Ontario residents: Must be registered as a member in good standing with the CPSO. Applicants not registered with this college will not be considered. For residents of other provinces and the United States: Must be willing to register with CPSO and relocate to Ontario.
Depth and breadth of knowledge, skills, and expertise in psychodynamic/psychoanalytic therapy. This could include Jungian analysis, Adlerian analysis, or any other psychodynamic/psychoanalytic approach. This could be obtained through one or more of the following: personal experience in receiving psychodynamic/psychoanalytic therapy, individual research and interest, education, clinical expertise, training, and supervision.
Please note that while our clinic is dedicated exclusively to psychodynamic and psychoanalytic modalities, some patients who begin psychotherapy sessions may benefit more from other modalities before commencing analytical work due to their current symptoms. Such modalities include cognitive-behavioural or other non-analytic approaches. As such, we welcome practitioners who work with experiential and integrative approaches within a psychodynamic/psychoanalytic framework.
Experience and comfort with virtual therapy and working with adolescents and adults.

Assets:

Experience with couples, families, pre-/post-natal/postpartum issues, women-specific issues, or eating disorders.
Experience working with children and teenagers under 16.
Knowledge of Bowen Family Systems theory.
French or additional language skills.

Availability: Monday to Friday, including mornings, afternoons, and evenings.




Please note:

This is an independent contractor position.
Only applicants who are selected for further consideration will be contacted. We appreciate your interest in joining our team!

Application Deadline: Open until the position is filled. Early applications are encouraged.




We look forward to welcoming a passionate and skilled psychotherapist to our team!




The Centre for Psychodynamic Insights is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment where all employees and patients feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workplace that reflects the diversity of our patients and the communities in which we live and serve. If you require accommodation for any stage of the recruitment process/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations), please reach out to us at ***@centreforpsychodynamicinsights.com (🔒 Premium).




Intelligence Disclosure

The Centre for Psychodynamic Insights does not use artificial intelligence tools to screen or automatically evaluate applicants. All applications are reviewed by the Clinic Director and administrative team.

jobs.full_description_text:
Key information on opportunity:

• Virtual appointments only

• Schedule is flexible (your choice)

• Approximately 6-8 hours/week with opportunity to increase if you desire

• No admin work, you just have to document your consultations

• Billings: estimated billings $500/hour net to you (OHIP)

 

Position Overview:

We are looking for an psychiatrist with excellent people skills to do brief one-time consults. The physician will be evaluating for the patients suitability for CBT and CBT-i.

 

Time commitment: 6-8 hours per week. Opportunity to add more hours available if interested.

 

Income:

• Estimated billings $500/hour net to you (OHIP, no HST charged)

 

Location: Virtual, appointments done over OTN.

 

Hours: flexible

 

Admin: Complete Admin support. No admin work - you just have to complete your notes (Accuro EMR) - several templates to choose from and can help you create your own. Extensive questionnaires are already completed prior to appointments to cut down on charting and we can help you create the ones you would like.

 

Requirements: Licensed to practice medicine in Ontario

 

About the clinic:

Institute for Behavioural & Functional Medicine offers behavioural & lifestyle interventions to help patients retraining their physiology to correct chronic health problems. We offer evidence-based, OHIP-funded rehabilitation programs like CBT-i, CBT, CPT, mindfulness and CBT for somatization. The first consultation is with the physician to evaluate for a patient's suitability for beginning psychological rehabilitation of their chronic condition. The 2nd appointment is with the GP Psychotherapist to prepare for the OHIP funded counselling. Learn more about this rapidly expanding field at ibfmed.ca.

jobs.full_description_text:
About the Clinic

An innovative ADHD clinic is seeking a collaborative, patient-focused Psychiatrist to join their multidisciplinary team. This role supports a wide range of clinical presentations, including ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), and co-occurring conditions such as anxiety, depression, mood disorders, and trauma. 




In this role, you will:

Conduct psychiatric consultations (A195/K630) for adults as part of their assessment and treatment model 
Collaborate closely with psychologists and psychological associates as part of a comprehensive assessment process, with shared clinical insight informing consensus diagnosis and recommendations 
Provide consultations independently based on referrals from primary care providers 
Provide short-term follow-up care for both new and returning patients 
Work both on-site at their Toronto clinic and remotely 

All patients are referred by a primary care physician. 




Requirements

A collaborative mindset and genuine interest in multidisciplinary care
Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Licensed and in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) 
Fellow of the Royal College of Physicians of Canada (FRCPC) in Psychiatry 
Authorized to work with adult populations (required) 
Experience working with ASD is considered an asset

Commitment & Compensatio​n

1 day per week (6–8 hour clinic), with opportunity to increase 
Retain 100% of OHIP billings 
No clinic overhead fees 
$225/hour for non-OHIP-covered work (e.g., internal collaboration, documentation) 
No-shows compensated at OHIP rates
Comprehensive administrative support provided
Retention Bonus:
$2,500 after 6 months 
$2,500 after 12 months
